segments.zh: 冲进房间，没有真正正确地自我介绍，就直接走向冰箱，

segments.ko: And, you know, we just thought, who is this guy?  But I have to say he was an interesting man,
segments.zh: 而且，你知道，我们只是想，这个人是谁？  但我不得不说他是一个有趣的人

segments.ko: quite a charming man. This is what I was  thinking at the time. And he popped it open.

segments.ko: He said, we have reason to celebrate. He was an  English guy. We've got a reason to celebrate.

segments.ko: And I don't know, I felt like he was trying  to sell us something or I don't know what was going on. But it turned out that this  guy's name was John Hammond. Right.
segments.zh: 我不知道，我觉得他想向我们推销一些东西，或者我不知道发生了什么事。但事实证明，这个人的名字叫约翰·哈蒙德。正确的。

segments.ko: And he was a billionaire. OK,  and, you know, billionaires, what can you do? I mean, they just think  that they run the world. They think they
segments.zh: 他是一位亿万富翁。好吧，亿万富翁们，你们知道，你们能做什么？我的意思是，他们只是认为他们统治着世界。他们认为他们

segments.ko: own the world and they probably  do, don't they? Let's be honest.

segments.ko: But this guy, John Hammond was a billionaire and  he started to tell us about this extraordinary
segments.zh: 但这个人，约翰·哈蒙德是一位亿万富翁，他开始向我们讲述这个非凡的事

segments.ko: thing that he'd done. I mean, I don't know how  it was possible. I mean, it was mind blowing.
segments.zh: 他所做的事。我的意思是，我不知道这怎么可能。我的意思是，这真是令人兴奋。

segments.ko: I still can't quite come to terms with it  now. Basically, what he told us is that
segments.zh: 我现在还不能完全接受它。基本上，他告诉我们的是

segments.zh: 他在哥斯达黎加海岸附近的这个岛上有一个项目。是的，他拥有这座岛。

segments.zh: 他当然做到了。他是一位亿万富翁。在那个岛上，他正在做一些有趣的事情。

segments.ko: Now, I know what you're going to say. This sounds,  this sounds suspicious. Who is this guy? OK,

segments.zh: 我的意思是，我有点怀疑，但他说得越多，事情就变得越有趣。

segments.ko: Let me try to get to the point. He told us that on this island he was developing actual  dinosaurs. He was breeding dinosaurs.
segments.zh: 让我试着切入主题。他告诉我们，他正在这个岛上培育真正的恐龙。他正在培育恐龙。

segments.ko: Ellie and I were both  shocked. Sort of incredulous, like we couldn't quite believe it, but  also fascinated because, as you know,
segments.zh: 艾莉和我都感到震惊。有点难以置信，就像我们不太相信它一样，但也很着迷，因为如你所知，

segments.ko: for a palaeontologist, the idea that someone  had been genetically engineering and breeding
segments.zh: 对于古生物学家来说，某人进行基因工程和育种的想法

segments.ko: real living dinosaurs was irresistible.  I mean, this was just irresistible to us.
segments.zh: 真实存在的恐龙是不可抗拒的。  我的意思是，这对我们来说是不可抗拒的。

segments.ko: And this man, John Hammond, told us  that he developed this park. It was going to be a theme park, a bit like  sort of Disneyland or or, you know,
segments.zh: 这个人，约翰·哈蒙德，告诉我们他开发了这个公园。这将是一个主题公园，有点像迪士尼乐园，或者，你知道，

segments.ko: those those theme parks where they have  dolphins and killer whales who do tricks, you know, that sort of thing.  Sea Life Centre or something.
segments.zh: 那些主题公园里有海豚和虎鲸，它们会表演特技，你知道的，诸如此类的事情。  海洋生物中心什么的。

segments.ko: But it was for dinosaurs. And the insurance  guy told us that they'd had some problem, one of the, one of the members of staff,  that there'd been a health and safety
segments.zh: 但这是为了恐龙。保险人员告诉我们，他们遇到了一些问题，其中一名工作人员，健康和安全方面存在问题

segments.ko: issue and that they needed experts  to come just to check the island, just to make sure that it was it was safe  and that it could then be opened. It was
segments.zh: 问题，他们需要专家来检查该岛，以确保它是安全的，然后可以打开它。原来是

segments.ko: And we had been chosen. Ellie and I had  been handpicked by John Hammond and his company and his insurance man. They'd chosen us.
segments.zh: 我们被选中了。艾莉和我是约翰·哈蒙德和他的公司以及他的保险公司精心挑选的。他们选择了我们。

segments.ko: They'd heard about our reputation  as being leading paleo. What was

segments.zh: 它？古生物学家和古植物学家。所以很高兴被这个选择

segments.ko: this billionaire to go and  take part in this project.
segments.zh: 这位亿万富翁要去参加这个项目。

segments.ko: And so despite the fact we had the  dig and everything, we thought, well, this is this is extraordinary.  We have to go. So we agreed.
segments.zh: 因此，尽管我们已经进行了挖掘和一切，但我们认为，嗯，这真是太棒了。  我们得走了。所以我们同意了。

segments.ko: I mean, I was a little sceptical. I thought this  there's got to be a catch here somewhere. But we went and, you know, we took a  helicopter flight and everything.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，我有点怀疑。我想这一定是有什么问题。但我们去了，你知道，我们乘坐了直升机等等。

segments.ko: It was very exciting. And  obviously it was just wonderful to have the experience with Ellie. And  we landed on the island and I was,
segments.zh: 非常令人兴奋。显然，和艾莉在一起的经历真是太棒了。我们降落在岛上，我，

segments.ko: you know, both of us looking out of the  window to see if we could see anything.
segments.zh: 你知道，我们俩都看着窗外，看看是否能看到什么。

segments.zh: 他一直说“我们不遗余力”，他们一定花了很多钱。他还告诉我们有一家公司参与其中。本来不是，

segments.zh: 他不是这个项目的唯一投资者。

segments.ko: There was another company called InGen, I  think it was, who had also invested money in this project. It was… astronomical amounts  of investment had been put into this project.
segments.zh: 我认为还有一家名为国际遗传公司（InGen）的公司也为这个项目投资了资金。这是……这个项目投入了天文数字的投资。

segments.ko: The insurance man told us about,  you know, some of the investors.
segments.zh: 保险公司的人告诉我们一些投资者的情况。

segments.ko: I mean, to be honest, that stuff  is pretty boring to me. So a lot of it went over my head. I was just  thinking, let me see the dinosaurs.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，说实话，这些东西对我来说很无聊。所以很多事情都超出了我的理解范围。我只是想，让我看看恐龙。

segments.ko: You know, I kind of didn't believe it. I was  thinking what, maybe they, maybe they've got, I don't know, a couple of little ones.  Maybe they're just I don't know what,
segments.zh: 你知道，我有点不相信。我在想，也许他们，也许他们有，我不知道，几个小孩子。  也许他们只是我不知道什么，

segments.ko: I didn't know what to think. Birds dressed  as dinosaurs, who knows? I was just curious.
segments.zh: 我不知道该怎么想。鸟儿装扮成恐龙，谁知道呢？我只是好奇。

segments.ko: So we arrived on the island and the  first thing that John Hammond… I mean, we were tired. It was a long journey.
segments.zh: 所以我们到达了岛上，约翰·哈蒙德做的第一件事就是……我的意思是，我们累了。这是一段漫长的旅程。

segments.zh: 但他坚持要做的第一件事就是带我们游览岛屿。于是我们就出发了。他真的让我们神魂颠倒。

segments.ko: And we were in these really nice  looking Jeeps riding through, driving through the island. I was thinking,  OK, I'll see it. I'll believe it when I see
segments.zh: 我们乘坐这些非常漂亮的吉普车穿过岛屿。我在想，好吧，我会看看的。当我看到时我就会相信

segments.ko: it. That was what I was thinking. I'll believe  it when I see actual dinosaurs driving along.
segments.zh: 它。这就是我的想法。当我看到真正的恐龙在行驶时我就会相信这一点。

segments.ko: Ellie started to notice the plant life. And she  was saying, “look at these plants. These are,
segments.zh: 艾莉开始注意到植物的生命。她说，“看看这些植物。这些是，

segments.ko: these are, these are actually original. These  are the same plants that we've seen in fossil
segments.zh: 这些是，这些实际上是原创的。这些植物与我们在化石中看到的植物相同

segments.ko: records. This is incredible.” And John Hammond, of  course, was saying, “oh, yes, we've included lots
segments.zh: 记录。这太不可思议了。”当然，约翰·哈蒙德说，“哦，是的，我们已经包括了很多

segments.zh: 您确切地知道我们是如何做到这一切的。我们不遗余力”，艾莉被这些植物分散了注意力。

segments.ko: And then as we drove up this hill, that  is when I caught my first sight of the
segments.zh: 然后当我们开车上这座山时，我第一次看到了

segments.ko: most incredible thing I've ever  seen in my life, at that point.
segments.zh: 那时，这是我一生中见过的最不可思议的事情。

segments.ko: There they were. Three, if I remember correctly, Brachiosaurus. Full size. I mean, these  things are like the size of skyscrapers
segments.zh: 他们就在那里。三，如果我没记错的话，腕龙。全尺寸。我的意思是，这些东西就像摩天大楼那么大

segments.ko: with huge long necks walking in a line,  calling to each other. I was stunned.
segments.zh: 巨大的长脖子排成一排，互相呼唤。我惊呆了。

segments.ko: When when I managed to… Ellie  didn't. I was saying, “Ellie, look at this. Look, look, look.” She was…  she's a paleobotanist. She loves plants.
segments.zh: 当我成功时……艾莉没有。我说，“艾莉，看看这个。看，看，看。”她是……她是一位古植物学家。她喜欢植物。

segments.ko: But I managed to get her to look in the same  direction as me and she couldn't believe it,
segments.zh: 但我设法让她看向与我相同的方向，她简直不敢相信，

segments.ko: too. And I know we'd, we we couldn't help it.  We got out of the Jeeps and walked towards them.
segments.zh: 也。我知道我们会这么做，我们无能为力。  我们下了吉普车，朝他们走去。

segments.ko: I mean, thinking back on it now, that was  probably not a very wise idea. If you see three
segments.zh: 我的意思是，现在回想起来，这可能不是一个非常明智的想法。如果你看到三个

segments.zh: 巨大的动物有教堂那么大，直接走到它们身边可能不是一个好主意。

segments.ko: But we were so excited and I was  amazed to actually see the actual, the bone structure, the way that  they moved. It was indescribable.
segments.zh: 但我们非常兴奋，我很惊讶能够真正看到真实的骨骼结构和它们移动的方式。这是难以形容的。

segments.ko: And it's unreal to me now to imagine  the sequence of events that happened afterwards and it all happened so  quickly. But that was incredible.
segments.zh: 现在我很难想象随后发生的一系列事件，而且这一切都发生得如此之快。但这太不可思议了。

segments.zh: 但约翰说，“回到吉普车里去。我们还有很多其他的东西要看。这只是开始。”

segments.zh: 我们继续前行，然后在山谷中看到了成群的副栉龙。我从来没能做到

segments.zh: 这么说。这些恐龙成群地穿过山谷，在水中进食。

segments.ko: I mean, absolutely mind blowing stuff.  Eventually, we we kept travelling by Jeep. And
segments.zh: 我的意思是，绝对令人兴奋的东西。  最终，我们继续乘坐吉普车旅行。和

segments.zh: 它看起来好像生病了。有一些工作人员在那里照顾它。所以我们走过去发现那是一只三角龙，一只真正的三角龙，

segments.ko: the most beautiful triceratops, so much  more beautiful than I'd ever imagined.
segments.zh: 最美丽的三角龙，比我想象的还要美丽。

segments.zh: 但这只躺着，显然病了。身体不舒服。我们怎么知道的？嗯，旁边有一座恐龙粪便山。

segments.zh: 在此之后一定要洗手，因为你永远不知道。她很着迷。

segments.zh: 哈蒙德说：“来吧，我们必须继续前进。”艾莉决定留下来

segments.zh: 三角龙。她想尝试帮助这只生病的三角龙。所以她决定留下来。

segments.zh: 那是艾莉。她一直都是这样。你知道，如果她决定做某事，她就会去做，你无能为力。只是

segments.zh: 但无论如何，我和哈蒙德以及他的保险人员一起回到了吉普车，我想他的名字叫唐纳德。唐纳德·杰拉诺。就是这样。根纳罗……瓜尔诺？

segments.ko: like John Hammond was just ticking boxes. Yeah,  palaeontologist inspection, fine, whatever.
segments.zh: 就像约翰·哈蒙德只是在方框里打勾一样。是的，古生物学家检查，好吧，无论如何。

segments.ko: There was another scientist  there as well. His name was, what was his name? Ian, Ian Malcolm,  Ian Malcolm, interesting character, Ian.
segments.zh: 那里还有另一位科学家。他的名字是，他叫什么名字？伊恩，伊恩·马尔科姆，伊恩·马尔科姆，有趣的人物，伊恩。

segments.ko: Now Ian was not a palaeontologist. He was,  well, he described himself as a chaotician, a chaotician. That's someone who  is an expert in chaos theory,
segments.zh: 现在伊恩不再是古生物学家了。他是，嗯，他形容自己是一个混乱者，一个混乱者。那是混沌理论专家，

segments.ko: which, I mean, it's a branch of maths, basically.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，它基本上是数学的一个分支。

segments.ko: I mean, to be honest, Ian, he  was a very flamboyant character, which you don't expect really from a  mathematician, do you? I mean, really,
segments.zh: 我的意思是，说实话，伊恩，他是一个非常浮夸的人物，你不会真正期望数学家有这样的性格，不是吗？我的意思是，真的，

segments.ko: I wasn't that impressed by Ian, to be  honest. I mean, he was a, he was very, what's the word for it? He was very eccentric  and flamboyant and didn't really act like a,
segments.zh: 老实说，我对伊恩印象并不深刻。我的意思是，他是，他非常，这个词是什么？他非常古怪、浮夸，表现得并不像，

segments.ko: he was very happy to be known as a chaotician.  He was always telling, oh yeah, I'm a chaotician,
segments.zh: 他很高兴被称为混沌者。  他总是说，哦，是的，我是一个混乱主义者，

segments.ko: I study chaos theory. You know what chaos theory  is? Let me, let me show you with a drop of water.
segments.zh: 我研究混沌理论。你知道什么是混沌理论吗？让我，让我用一滴水给你看。

segments.ko: And I was thinking, this is all very vague to me  as a palaeontologist. It's never really been my, my cup of tea. Things like chaos theory, maths,
segments.zh: 我在想，作为一名古生物学家，这对我来说非常模糊。这从来都不是我真正喜欢的。比如混沌理论、数学、

segments.ko: just let me get into the ground and  actually get my hands on some dinosaur bones. That's my approach to this,  much more practical, but fine. Okay.
segments.zh: 让我深入地下，实际接触到一些恐龙骨头。这就是我的方法，更实用，但也很好。好的。

segments.ko: For some reason, Ian, as a chaotician, as  a mathematician had been brought to inspect the Island. I mean, what, I don't know what,  I don't know if he was qualified to do that,
segments.zh: 出于某种原因，伊恩作为混沌学家、数学家被带去考察这座岛屿。我的意思是，什么，我不知道什么，我不知道他是否有资格这样做，

segments.ko: but anyway, he was interesting company and Ellie  certainly seemed to seem to like him. Yeah.
segments.zh: 但无论如何，他是一个有趣的伙伴，艾莉似乎很喜欢他。是的。

segments.ko: I mean, as far as I'm concerned, he  was just a jumped-up maths teacher, really, who wore dark glasses and a  shirt unbuttoned and very handsome.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，就我而言，他只是一个跳起来的数学老师，真的，戴着墨镜，衬衫解开扣子，非常英俊。

segments.ko: Anyway, Ian was there. We all sat down to  eat. I mean, I, I wasn't particularly hungry.
segments.zh: 不管怎样，伊恩就在那里。我们都坐下来吃饭。我是说，我，我不是特别饿。

segments.ko: I mean, I'd lost my appetite to be honest,  but we sat round and ate and talked and discussed stuff. And Ian made some, some  interesting points about the ethics of it.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，说实话，我已经失去了胃口，但我们围坐在一起吃饭、聊天、讨论事情。伊恩就其道德问题提出了一些有趣的观点。

segments.ko: Um, I mean, what a, what a deep thinker  he is. “Oh, you thought about, you know, your scientists have been so busy.”  Uh, what was it again? What did he
segments.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，他是一个多么、多么深刻的思想家。 “哦，你想过，你知道，你们的科学家一直很忙。”  呃，又是什么？他做了什么

segments.ko: say? “Your scientists have been so  busy trying to work out whether you could do this. They didn't think about  whether they should.” Deep, deep stuff.
segments.zh: 说？ “你们的科学家一直忙于弄清楚你们是否可以做到这一点。他们没有考虑是否应该这样做。”很深很深的东西。

segments.ko: I don't know but that's what he  brought to the meeting. Anyway, it didn't seem to make any difference. Like,
segments.zh: 我不知道，但这就是他带来会议的内容。无论如何，似乎没有什么区别。喜欢，

segments.ko: to be honest, any of the things that we said  or observed didn't seem to make any difference.
segments.zh: 老实说，我们所说或观察到的任何事情似乎都没有任何影响。

segments.ko: I think John Hammond had basically  decided that he was going to do this and that he had the money. He had  the influence. It was going to happen.
segments.zh: 我认为约翰·哈蒙德基本上已经决定他要这样做并且他有钱。他有影响力。它即将发生。

segments.ko: And the insurance company just needed to  tick boxes. They needed to prove that they got some experts in to just verify that  the park was safe. I mean, I don't know.
segments.zh: 保险公司只需勾选复选框即可。他们需要证明他们聘请了一些专家来验证公园是否安全。我的意思是，我不知道。

segments.ko: I think it's completely impossible to  check that the park was safe. And anyway, as we know the park, well, was it safe?  No, it wasn't. It was not safe at all.
segments.zh: 我认为检查公园是否安全是完全不可能的。不管怎样，据我们所知，公园安全吗？  不，不是。根本不安全。

segments.ko: Let me tell you exactly what happened. So  after that, they showed us the laboratories where they developed these dinosaurs and  they told us how they'd done it. And it's,
segments.zh: 让我告诉你到底发生了什么。之后，他们向我们展示了他们培育这些恐龙的实验室，并告诉我们他们是如何做到的。这是，

segments.ko: it is actually fascinating  and incredible what they did.
segments.zh: 他们所做的事情实际上令人着迷且令人难以置信。

segments.ko: So they, how did they get the dinosaur DNA? Well,
segments.zh: 那么他们，他们是怎么得到恐龙DNA的呢？出色地，

segments.ko: Hammond had found amber in the ground.  Amber, not Amber, not my friend Amber,
segments.zh: 哈蒙德在地下发现了琥珀。  琥珀，不是琥珀，不是我的朋友琥珀，

segments.ko: but amber, you know, it's like a dried  sap that comes out of a tree. Okay.
segments.zh: 但是琥珀，你知道，它就像从树上流出来的干汁液。好的。

segments.ko: You know, trees, inside trees, they have this  stuff called sap. It's kind of like a sugary, sweet, gloopy sort of liquid, which  if you, certain trees have a lot of
segments.zh: 你知道，树，在树里面，有一种叫做树液的东西。它有点像一种含糖的、甜的、粘稠的液体，如果你，某些树有很多

segments.ko: sap inside them. It's kind of like  the blood of a tree, let's say.
segments.zh: 它们里面的汁液。可以说，它有点像树的血。

segments.ko: And, and certain trees, like I think pine  trees, some types of pine trees, I think, I mean, I'm a palaeontologist.  I'm not, I'm not a botanist. So,
segments.zh: 而且，某些树木，比如我认为的松树，某些类型的松树，我想，我的意思是，我是一名古生物学家。  我不是，我不是植物学家。所以，

segments.ko: you know, don't expect me to  know everything about everything.
segments.zh: 你知道，别指望我无所不知。

segments.ko: Um, but they, the sap comes  out and it drips out and it, it sometimes quite quickly will drip down  the trunk of a tree. And for example,
segments.zh: 嗯，但是，树液流出来，滴下来，有时很快就会从树干上滴下来。例如，

segments.ko: if there are insects just sitting on the tree,  sometimes they will be trapped inside this amber,
segments.zh: 如果树上有昆虫，有时它们会被困在琥珀里，

segments.ko: trapped inside and the amber then sets and  it goes hard. And if it falls on the ground, it could be buried and it can actually  last for millions and millions of years.
segments.zh: 被困在里面，琥珀就会凝固，变硬。如果它掉到地上，它可能会被掩埋，而且它实际上可以持续数百万年。

segments.ko: And John Hammond had been searching all around  the world for samples of this amber because
segments.zh: 约翰·哈蒙德一直在世界各地寻找这种琥珀的样本，因为

segments.ko: him [he] and his scientists had worked out that  actually some of the insects preserved inside
segments.zh: 他[他]和他的科学家们发现，实际上，里面保存着一些昆虫

segments.ko: the amber could contain not only their own DNA,  but the DNA of other animals, and insects that
segments.zh: 琥珀不仅含有它们自己的 DNA，还含有其他动物和昆虫的 DNA

segments.ko: bite specifically mosquitoes, because as we all  know, mosquitoes bite, don't they? They bite, they draw blood from animals like us or  indeed many other species of animals and
segments.zh: 专门叮咬蚊子，因为众所周知，蚊子会叮人，不是吗？它们会咬人，从像我们这样的动物或许多其他种类的动物身上抽取血液，

segments.ko: they keep the blood inside them and they  feed on it. Incredibly, John had, and his
segments.zh: 它们将血液保留在体内并以此为食。令人难以置信的是，约翰和他的

segments.ko: scientists and his teams had found perfectly  preserved mosquitoes full of dinosaur blood.
segments.zh: 科学家和他的团队发现了保存完好、充满恐龙血液的蚊子。

segments.ko: These are mosquitoes that had been preserved  in amber from the Jurassic period. They'd extracted the DNA. It must have taken  them such a long time, but as he said,
segments.zh: 这些蚊子保存在侏罗纪时期的琥珀中。他们提取了 DNA。他们一定花了很长时间，但正如他所说，

segments.ko: they spared no expense, extracted the DNA  from the stomachs of these mosquitoes.
segments.zh: 他们不惜重金，从这些蚊子的胃里提取了DNA。

segments.ko: And in there, in that blood, they found yes,  DNA, dinosaur DNA. And from that they cloned,
segments.zh: 在那里，在血液中，他们发现了 DNA，恐龙 DNA。由此他们克隆了，

segments.ko: they had cloned, I don't know exactly how they  do it, but they cloned dinosaurs and started
segments.zh: 他们克隆了，我不知道他们到底是怎么做到的，但他们克隆了恐龙并开始

segments.ko: to produce real dinosaurs. I don't know how, how  is that possible? I don't really understand it, but their, their lead geneticist,  Henry Wu told us all about it.
segments.zh: 生产真正的恐龙。我不知道怎么办，这怎么可能？我不太明白，但是他们的首席遗传学家亨利·吴告诉了我们这一切。

segments.ko: A lot of it did go over my head, but  they showed us, I don't know how, like the, what do you do? Create a dinosaur  first and then it lays eggs and new dinosaurs
segments.zh: 很多事情确实超出了我的想象，但他们向我们展示了，我不知道如何，比如，你做什么？首先创造一只恐龙，然后它产蛋和新的恐龙

segments.ko: arrive? I don't know how, but they had an  egg. They showed us an egg in an incubator, an egg about the size of a rugby ball  and it hatched right in front of us.
segments.zh: 到达？我不知道怎么回事，但他们有一个鸡蛋。他们向我们展示了孵化器中的一枚鸡蛋，一枚橄榄球大小的鸡蛋，它就在我们面前孵化了。

segments.ko: And we saw a dinosaur popping  out and I identified it. It was, as I expected, it was an actual Velociraptor,
segments.zh: 我们看到一只恐龙突然出现，我认出了它。正如我所料，它是一只真正的迅猛龙，

segments.ko: a little Velociraptor baby popping out of the  shell. And it was, well, a combination of,
segments.zh: 一只小迅猛龙宝宝破壳而出。它是，嗯，的组合，

segments.ko: on one hand, cute and adorable and fascinating,  and on the other hand, absolutely terrifying.
segments.zh: 一方面，可爱、可爱、迷人，但另一方面，又绝对可怕。

segments.ko: A whirlwind of emotions and  feelings flew through my head. I didn't really have time to process it all.
segments.zh: 一股情绪和感受的旋风掠过我的脑海。我真的没有时间处理这一切。

segments.ko: It all happened so quickly, but there they, there  they, there they had Velociraptors. And I said, wait a minute, what other, what  other predators have you got? Do you,
segments.zh: 这一切发生得太快了，但是他们，他们，他们有迅猛龙。我说，等一下，你还有什么其他掠食者？你，

segments.ko: do you have a Tyrannosaurus Rex? And  Hammond was delighted to announce, “yes, we have a T-Rex.” I couldn't  wait to see it. I'll be honest.
segments.zh: 你有霸王龙吗？哈蒙德很高兴地宣布：“是的，我们有一只霸王龙。”我迫不及待地想看到它。我会说实话。

segments.ko: Little did I know how much of it  I would actually see. But they also told us that they didn't have the  full genetic code for these dinosaurs,
segments.zh: 我几乎不知道我实际上会看到多少。但他们也告诉我们，他们没有这些恐龙的完整遗传密码，

segments.ko: that the genetic information  they had was about 98% complete.
segments.zh: 他们拥有的遗传信息大约有 98% 完整。

segments.ko: Again, I'm not a geneticist, geneticist, so  I don't really understand it. But what they
segments.zh: 再说一次，我不是遗传学家，所以我不太明白。但他们什么

segments.ko: did apparently is to, to complete the genetic  code, genetic makeup. So they’d got a hundred
segments.zh: 显然所做的就是，完成遗传密码，基因构成。所以他们有一百个

segments.ko: percent. So they could actually continue cloning  the dinosaurs. They had to take the remaining 2%
segments.zh: 百分比。所以他们实际上可以继续克隆恐龙。他们必须拿走剩下的2%

segments.ko: of genes that they missed. And they took it  from like the closest thing they could find.
segments.zh: 他们错过的基因。他们从他们能找到的最接近的东西中获取了它。

segments.ko: And in this case, that was frogs.  So they took 2% frog DNA and added it to the 98% dinosaur DNA. And that  allowed them to clone the dinosaur.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，那就是青蛙。  因此，他们提取了 2% 的青蛙 DNA，并将其添加到 98% 的恐龙 DNA 中。这使得他们能够克隆恐龙。

segments.ko: So, I mean, the dinosaurs that we saw, they  didn't look very froggy. So I don't know quite exactly where that, I didn't at the  time know where that 2% frog DNA was really
segments.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我们看到的恐龙，它们看起来不太像青蛙。所以我不太清楚它在哪里，我当时不知道那 2% 的青蛙 DNA 到底在哪里

segments.ko: going in terms of the dinosaurs, because they  looked very dinosaur-ish to me. I know that's not a scientific term, dinosaur-ish, but  I'm just trying to put it in terms that,
segments.zh: 就恐龙而言，因为它们在我看来非常像恐龙。我知道这不是一个科学术语，类似于恐龙，但我只是想用这样的术语来表达：

segments.ko: you know, the lay person would understand,  because I'm assuming you're not a, an expert.
segments.zh: 你知道，外行人会理解，因为我假设你不是专家。

segments.ko: So I've learned in my years  of being a palaeontologist, I learned when I was a palaeontologist that  you have to talk to the public as you know,
segments.zh: 所以我在担任古生物学家的这些年里了解到，当我还是一名古生物学家时，我了解到你必须与公众交谈，如你所知，

segments.ko: in terms that they will understand. So  forgive me for using non-scientific language, but you understand. So I don't know, they  didn't look very frog-ish, these dinosaurs.
segments.zh: 用他们会理解的术语。所以请原谅我使用非科学语言，但你明白。所以我不知道，这些恐龙看起来不太像青蛙。

segments.ko: They looked exactly like the dinosaurs as we  expected they would look based on the research
segments.zh: 它们看起来和恐龙一模一样，正如我们根据研究预期的那样

segments.ko: that we'd done. So I was very happy to, to,  to see that our research was accurate mostly, but I was curious about this 2% frog  DNA. It wasn't obvious at the beginning.
segments.zh: 我们已经做到了。所以我很高兴看到我们的研究大部分都是准确的，但我对这 2% 的青蛙 DNA 很好奇。一开始并不明显。

segments.ko: I'll come back to that. Now, the next thing that  happened is that someone came in the room in the
segments.zh: 我会回到这个话题。现在，接下来发生的事情是有人走进了房间

segments.ko: middle of this meeting, this discussion  we were having and said, Oh, Dr. Hammond, um, your guests have arrived. And I was  thinking, Oh, other guests. Excellent. Maybe
segments.zh: 在这次会议的中间，我们正在进行讨论，并说，哦，哈蒙德博士，嗯，您的客人已经到了。我在想，哦，还有其他客人。出色的。或许

segments.ko: we've got some other scientists, maybe some  more palaeontologists. I mean, hopefully it's
segments.zh: 我们还有其他一些科学家，也许还有更多古生物学家。我的意思是，希望是这样

segments.ko: not just some sort of rock star chaotician who,  you know, is just flirting with my girlfriend.
segments.zh: 不仅仅是某种摇滚明星混乱者，你知道，他只是在和我女朋友调情。

segments.ko: Maybe we'll have some proper palaeontologists  who I can, you know, uh, share my thoughts
segments.zh: 也许我们会有一些合适的古生物学家，我可以，你知道，呃，分享我的想法

segments.ko: with. We went through and lo and behold, was it  expert scientists? No, it was two children. Yeah.
segments.zh: 和。我们经历了，你瞧，这是专家科学家吗？不，是两个孩子。是的。

segments.ko: Always children. Why? I don't  understand. I still, to this day, don't understand why children always have  to be involved when there are dinosaurs.
segments.zh: 永远都是孩子。为什么？我不明白。直到今天，我仍然不明白为什么有恐龙的时候孩子们总是必须参与其中。

segments.ko: They're just keep the children  away from the dinosaurs. But no, John Hammond had invited his grandchildren to  come to the Island before it had been certified
segments.zh: 他们只是让孩子们远离恐龙。但不，约翰·哈蒙德在该岛获得认证之前就邀请他的孙子们来到该岛

segments.ko: safe. I mean, a very questionable man, John  Hammond, very, very questionable indeed.
segments.zh: 安全的。我的意思是，约翰·哈蒙德是一个非常值得怀疑的人，确实非常非常值得怀疑。

segments.ko: And I mean, he's facing, obviously now, I  don't know if you've heard about all of the, all of the legal issues and things like  that, but he's, he is facing a lot of
segments.zh: 我的意思是，他现在显然面临着，我不知道你是否听说过所有所有的法律问题和类似的事情，但他面临着很多

segments.zh: 问责制。让这些亿万富翁保持一致很困难，不是吗？

segments.ko: But so he invited his grandchildren and  there they were Lex and Tim Lex and Tim, and everyone was so glad to  see them. And Ellie, of course,
segments.zh: 但他邀请了他的孙子们，他们是莱克斯和蒂姆，莱克斯和蒂姆，每个人都很高兴见到他们。当然还有艾莉，

segments.ko: was so great because she's, she's not like  me. She's great with kids. She loves kids.
segments.zh: 太棒了，因为她和我不一样。她对孩子们很好。她喜欢孩子。

segments.ko: And I mean, at the time, if I  can just share, I guess with you, at the time we were having this, not  an argument, we were talking about,
segments.zh: 我的意思是，当时，如果我能与你分享，我想，当时我们正在讨论这个问题，而不是争论，我们正在谈论，

segments.ko: you know, we were talking about  whether we should have children.
segments.zh: 你知道，我们正在讨论我们是否应该生孩子。

segments.ko: She wanted kids. And I was like, no, I'm, I  just like to dig things in the ground, you know,
segments.zh: 她想要孩子。我当时想，不，我，我只是喜欢在地里挖东西，你知道，

segments.ko: dig old dead animals out of the ground, and  children... It was a bit of an issue between us.
segments.zh: 从地里挖出死去的老动物，还有孩子……这是我们之间的一个问题。

segments.ko: You know, that's Ellie. She's a loving, caring  woman who not only is interested in ancient life,
segments.zh: 你知道，那是艾莉。她是一位充满爱心、充满爱心的女性，不仅对古代生活感兴趣，

segments.ko: but wants to bring new life into the  world. And that was her point of view.
segments.zh: 但想给世界带来新的生命。这就是她的观点。
